Done. The export succeeded on the first execution.

**What I did**

- Wrote `out/T3/solution.py`, a plain torch plus safetensors script. It loads both input shards, casts only the tensors matching an anchored regex for the seven per-layer projection modules to bfloat16, and leaves everything else float32 and untouched.
- Before writing, the script enforces the required checks and exits nonzero if any fails: exactly 112 bfloat16 tensors, layer 0 q_proj is bfloat16, embed_tokens is float32, 114 tensors total, unchanged name set, unchanged shapes, and bit-exact float32 values.
- Sharding is greedy first-fit in sorted name order with a 256 MiB tensor-data budget. The two 412 MB tensors each get their own shard. After writing, the script re-reads every shard and verifies dtypes, values, index mapping and per-shard budget.

**Result**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Shards written | 10 |
| Tensors | 114 |
| bfloat16 tensors | 112 |
| Executions | 1, no failures |

Shards 1 and 2 hold lm_head and embed_tokens alone. Shards 3 through 10 each hold exactly 256 MiB of bfloat16 projection data.

The self-report is at `out/T3/REPORT.md`. It notes one unclear point in the task: the packing order for shards is unspecified, so I used sorted name order, which the grader's stated rules should accept regardless of assignment.
